purpose: camera and chassis-tag accounting for experiment 7b565e2a, from the runner's own frame index and tag watch. Every frame's sha256 is in run1/frame_index.jsonl; the loose JPEGs are gitignored and bundled.
cameras_verdict: all three cameras recorded continuously for the whole window from the :8766 camera server, zero capture errors, every frame sha256 distinct, worst inter-frame gap 0.738 s against the 2 s staleness abort bound

chassis_tag_watch.plan_wording: 'the chassis tag moving relative to the floor tags in any camera WHEN TAGS ARE RESOLVABLE'; the saved plan also says the watch 'bounds gross motion only and the run does not depend on it - joint telemetry answers the pose-held question directly, as it did for L0'
chassis_tag_watch.why_disabled: the chassis tag was NOT resolvable when the pre-run baseline was taken (0 resolved samples), so there was no baseline to compare against and the runner recorded the condition as UNMEASURED rather than inventing one. It WAS resolvable 4 minutes earlier during the zero-motion dry run (1 sample at (470, 599) mm, yaw 80.9 deg), so this is a marginal-resolvability boundary at this pose, not a lighting or camera failure -- all three cameras kept serving fresh frames throughout.
chassis_tag_watch.verdict: UNMEASURED for this run. This is a real reduction in evidence against the L0 run, which had the watch enabled and clean at a 6.18 mm median offset, and it is reported rather than smoothed over. It does not weaken the run's own conclusion: the pose-held question is answered directly and more precisely by joint telemetry -- every measured non-L3 joint stayed within 0.439 deg of logical zero across all 1560 ticks against a 1.0 deg bound, and the pre- and post-run 18-servo samples are identical. IMU roll/pitch moved 0.10/0.07 deg against a 10 deg trip.

passive_recorder.note: the three markers (pre_run, protocol_tick0, post_run) were each accepted by the on-robot 50 Hz passive recorder with writer_alive true, and it reported queue_dropped 0 / capture_errors 0 / uncaptured_bytes 0 at every one, so the plan's persist-to-disk-during-the-run requirement is confirmed rather than assumed
